LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 4.1.2 CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.1: Listening and Speaking 4.1.2 Conversational skills
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 4.1.2 Conversational skills, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why are conversation skills important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 4.1.2 Conversational skills together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration-Speaking engagingly: The learner will speak engagingly as they simulate situations

relevant to the theme using informal register.

Values:
Integrity: The learner’s sense of honesty is heightened as they search online and offline focusing on ways of changing the

topic and giving and receiving feedback.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills and human sexuality-Peer pressure resistance: The learner is sensitised to resist peer pressure as they search online

and offline for ways of changing the topic and giving and receiving feedback.
